ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of the People's Republic of China on Anti-Money Laundering (2024 Amendment, effective January 1, 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 3, effective November 1, 2024); Implementing Rules on Customer Due Diligence for Financial Institutions (PBOC Order [2019] No. 1); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019, effective January 1, 2020); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective July 1, 2024).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Foreign Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, Registrar of Companies, or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing jurisdiction is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention: notarization if required at origin, then Apostille issued by the designated competent authority of the origin state; no further Chinese consular legalization. If the issuing jurisdiction is not an Apostille state: notarization at origin, then authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the origin state, then legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that state. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Foreign Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or equivalent official corporate registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if available in the issuing jurisdiction, stopping after the Apostille; otherwise consular legalization through the origin state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative routes, never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney Appointing the WFOE Incorporation Agent and Legal Representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign shareholder, duly notarized by a licensed notary in the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Hague Apostille state: notarization of the board resolution, followed by the Apostille certificate; no Chinese consular step. For a non-Hague state: notarization, then authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Use only the single path applicable to the origin jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Charter or Constitutional Documents) of the Foreign Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or authorized custodian of the foreign shareholder's constitutional records, with notarial certification where required
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the origin jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member, the certified copy must bear a Hague Apostille from the competent authority and no consular legalization. If not a member, the certified copy must pass through notarization, foreign ministry authentication, and Chinese consular legalization. These paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Foreign Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank of the foreign shareholder in the jurisdiction where the shareholder maintains its principal operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter must be notarized where the bank signs it, then either apostilled (if the bank's jurisdiction is an Apostille state) or authenticated by the foreign ministry and legalized by the Chinese embassy or consulate (if not an Apostille state). No document should receive both an apostille and a consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every beneficial owner, director, legal representative, and authorized signatory of the WFOE and its ultimate foreign shareholders must be screened at formation and thereafter on a risk refresh cycle of not more than 180 days against: (i) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (ii) the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (iii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (iv) the PRC anti-money laundering risk lists and administrative blacklists published by the People's Bank of China, the State Administration for Market Regulation, and the Ministry of Public Security; and (v) commercial PEP databases covering politically exposed persons. Any positive match must trigger enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth documentation, and senior management approval before incorporation proceeds. Even for a low-risk ISIC 4100-02 steel structure prefab EPC entity, the customer due diligence file must contain certified identity documents, an organizational chart, a UBO declaration, and corroborating beneficial ownership evidence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and the Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration System operated by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through provincial and municipal market regulation bureaus
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A WFOE must adopt a legal name in Simplified Chinese characters under the four-tier naming convention: administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or operational characteristics, and organizational form. An English name may be registered in parallel for banking, customs, and export contracts but does not replace the statutory Chinese name. Phonetic transliteration by pinyin is permitted for the distinctive trade name when derived from a foreign parent's corporate name, provided the transliteration does not mislead the public, violate public order, or conflict with prior registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must receive a written explanation referencing the statutory basis for refusal. The applicant may appeal by filing administrative reconsideration within 60 days from the date of the rejection notice with the market regulation authority at the next higher level, or may file an administrative lawsuit within 6 months in the competent People's Court. Before re-filing, legal counsel must analyze whether the rejection concerns prohibited tokens, misleading industry terms, conflict with a well-known mark, or similarity to an existing registered name. The applicant may also submit a corrected name through the same self-declaration system without losing the priority date if the correction is made before the original reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mail-drop address is not permissible for SAMR registration, tax confirmation, or corporate bank account opening in China. The WFOE must maintain a physical business place in mainland China evidenced by a lease agreement, title certificate, or sublease with valid landlord consent. For a steel structure prefab EPC company, the registered office may be an administrative head office, but a project site office alone is insufficient for company registration. Banks and tax authorities will reject postal-only addresses and commonly require site visits. A serviced office with physical meeting rooms, a local staff presence, and lawful sublease documentation is acceptable if the address is consistently displayed on corporate documents, invoices, and contracts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) legal name signboard must match the registered name and be displayed at the registered address; (2) original lease agreement, rent invoices, and landlord landlord identification must be available; (3) staff or legal representative must be present during normal business hours; (4) accounting ledgers, bank statements, VAT records, and social insurance filings must be accessible; (5) project-site construction permits, safety licenses, and EPC contracts must be retained; and (6) registered office must not be a bare virtual mailbox. Quantified risk: moderate, approximately 25% probability of an unannounced inspection in the first year after incorporation by municipal tax, market regulation, or fire-safety authorities, with higher likelihood in Zones with active tenancy audits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Blended hourly rates of partner, counsel, and paralegal time at prevailing Shanghai or Beijing market benchmarks for a standard WFOE formation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial serviced-office or registered-address service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark first-year serviced-office fee or registered-address service fee for a non-manufacturing administrative office.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial and consular fee schedules plus approved translation bureau tariff rates.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Relationship bank of the ultimate foreign shareholder

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government fee tariff: normally nil under the one-stop registration service; agency fees, if any, are separate and already included in corporate counsel fees.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective July 1, 2024), Articles 10-16, 23-31, 33-35, 47-49, 67-69 and 76; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 2, 4, 6 and 12; Interim Regulations on the Registration and Administration of Market Entities (State Council Decree 746), Articles 8, 15-17 and 22.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); local Market Regulation Administration (MRA) at the registered office; online enterprise registration service module under the SAMR national integrated service platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Company, together with the Articles of Association and the name reservation approval notice.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum registered capital for a WFOE limited liability company. The Articles must state the subscribed capital and the contribution schedule, and each shareholder must fully discharge its subscribed capital within five years after establishment per Article 47 of the Company Law. No blocked escrow account is required for standard WFOE formation; however, the foreign exchange capital account must receive the contribution before use, and construction qualification criteria may set higher working-capital or paid-in-capital thresholds.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 2025-01 OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [CN_WFOE_LTD] (THE COMPANY), unanimously adopted by written consent in accordance with the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Company's Articles of Association

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online services are handled through the Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) portal operated by STA and its provincial/municipal tax service bureaus; customs procedures for export clearance are administered by the General Administration of Customs of China.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign investor first incorporates the WFOE with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). The SAMR business license contains the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is automatically recognized as the taxpayer identification number (TIN) for corporate income tax, VAT, and withholding tax purposes. Tax registration is completed through the one-stop business registration process, after which the taxpayer obtains e-Tax login credentials and confirms tax registration details with the local STA tax service bureau. For a non-resident enterprise that has no establishment in China but derives China-source income, the non-resident taxpayer must register with the STA for tax withholding purposes and obtain a non-resident TIN via the e-Tax portal or through its withholding agent; treaty relief, where applicable, is claimed through the standard non-resident tax treaty procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity classification elections. A WFOE is classified as a Chinese resident enterprise under the Corporate Income Tax Law and is taxed at entity level on worldwide income; VAT general taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer status is an elective administrative registration, not an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Annual taxable turnover exceeding RMB 5,000,000 triggers mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration in China; entities with turnover at or below RMB 5,000,000 may retain small-scale taxpayer status unless they elect general taxpayer status. Export zero-rating and input VAT credit refunds require general taxpayer status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China requires VAT invoices to be issued through the STA electronic invoice service platform using Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice (FDEI) technology. General taxpayers must transmit invoice data in real time to the STA platform; each invoice receives a unique fiscal number, digital stamp, and anti-fraud validation. Enterprises may integrate their ERP systems with the e-invoice platform through approved APIs or portal-based workflows. Export sales must be supported by compliant zero-rated export invoices recorded in the same e-invoice system; the platform also performs automated cross-checks against customs export data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export sales of fabricated steel structure goods and components by a general VAT taxpayer qualify for 0% VAT zero-rating with entitlement to refund of attributable input VAT where: the goods are physically exported from China under an export customs declaration; the sale is made to an overseas customer under a genuine cross-border contract; the proceeds are received in foreign currency and repatriated to China; and the exporter retains complete customs, freight, and banking evidence. Cross-border construction services performed wholly outside China may also qualify for zero-rating or VAT exemption under the cross-border taxable services rules. Domestic on-site assembly, engineering design, and EPC services rendered inside China remain taxable at the applicable domestic rates, including 13% for goods and 9% for construction services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign exchange receipt
Zero-rated VAT export invoice and commercial invoice
Export sales contract and purchase order
Packing list and certificate of origin (where required)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to STA post-export verification and data matching with customs and foreign exchange records. If the export is found to be fictitious, goods fail to depart China, or foreign exchange proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory 180-day period, the STA will claw back any VAT exemption or refund, charge late payment interest, and impose penalties ranging from 50 percent to five times the tax under the Tax Administration Law. Customs penalties for false export declarations and smuggling liability under the Customs Law may also apply; deliberate fraudulent export refund claims are subject to criminal prosecution under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC), acting through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed floating exchange-rate regime under the PBOC/SAFE, with RMB fully convertible for genuine current-account transactions (goods trade, services, profit remittance) and restricted capital-account convertibility. A WFOE's registered capital injection is a capital-account flow and must be pre-filed with SAFE under the FDI foreign-exchange registration system; funds can be received only into an FDI capital account at a licensed domestic bank and each conversion from foreign currency to RMB is reviewed against the FDI business registration code. Shareholder loans require foreign-debt registration and macro-prudential limits. Profit remittance to the overseas parent is treated as a current-account dividend flow, but is permitted only after annual audit, corporate income tax final settlement, and submission of board resolution, audited financial statements and tax clearance certificate to the remitting bank. Practical operating hurdles include strict monitoring of capital-account funds against the approved business purpose, source-of-funds evidence for every remittance, and the fact that domestic RMB funds cannot be used for unauthorised offshore equity investment. Export revenues from steel structure EPC may be retained in foreign currency or converted to RMB; all FX transactions must be executed at the onshore market rate through a designated domestic bank. Overall, the current account is open and functional, while capital-account transactions require granular pre-registration and documentary banking controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's goods-trade monitoring, export proceeds must be repatriated to China and credited to the WFOE's domestic foreign-currency current account within the standard 90-day export collection window measured from the customs export declaration date; if payment terms extend beyond 90 days, the WFOE must file a deferred-receipt registration through its bank in advance. There is no mandatory conversion or surrender ratio in the current legal framework; the WFOE may retain 100% of its eligible export foreign-exchange proceeds in the domestic account or convert them to RMB at a designated bank. Advance receipts received more than 30 days before the export declaration also require a trade-credit report to the bank/SAFE monitoring system.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Escrow Account / Foreign Currency Current Account / RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account / Foreign Currency General Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore EMIs such as Airwallex, Payoneer and Revolut Business are not licensed by PBOC/SAFE as Chinese banks and are legally barred from servicing an onshore corporate account in the same manner as a licensed domestic bank. They may only operate as payment service providers through local licensed partners under SAFE's cross-border payment pilot, and even then they are viable only for auxiliary e-commerce collection or small working-capital flows, not for statutory FDI capital, settlement of EPC trade, or foreign debt. Therefore, as the primary treasury and clearing rail, their viability is Low; they should not be used as a substitute for a Tier-1 domestic bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PBOC anti-money-laundering regulations mandate face-to-face customer due diligence at the corporate account opening. For a WFOE, the statutory legal representative and the appointed signatory must generally attend the bank branch physically to execute account-opening documents, provide original valid identity documents, and undergo a compliance interview if requested. A remote consular proxy opening alone is not accepted: if the overseas legal representative cannot travel, he/she must execute a notarized power of attorney legalised by the PRC embassy/consulate, and the local authorised person must appear in person at the branch. The bank may also require a site visit to the registered address and an interview with the finance manager. In all cases, at least one physical appearance in China is effectively mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) opacity through multiple layers of offshore holding companies, making the ownership chain from the WFOE to natural persons unclear.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents for each entity in the ownership chain, including certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles, share register, directors register; notarized UBO declarations identifying every individual holding 25% or more; passport copies of all UBOs; an external-counsel-verified group organisation chart; and 12 months of parent bank statements or audited financial statements evidencing commercial substance and source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Primary source of funds for the Chinese registered capital injection and any shareholder loan is unclear, especially where remittances originate from a jurisdiction with bank secrecy or complex trust arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Personal and corporate source-of-funds statements; six to twelve months of bank statements leading to the remittance; sale agreements, dividend distribution minutes, liquidation or bonus certificates, or loan agreements; an independent asset/wealth report; tax clearance certificates from the remitting jurisdiction; and signed undertakings confirming no third-party funding and no money-laundering involvement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business purpose mismatch risk: the declared steel structure EPC / prefabricated steel building scope is not supported by operational substance, indicating shell-company or round-tripping risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE Foreign Investment Filing certificate; business license showing ISIC 4100-equivalent scopes; executed EPC contracts, purchase orders and project schedules; office lease, utility bills, employee social-insurance payment list and payroll records; on-site bank visit report; procurement invoices for steel and materials; and audited or management financials evidencing planned revenue and physical operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, sanctions or PEP exposure of ultimate shareholders or counterparties, including possible connections to restricted steel/export-controlled products or dual-use end-users.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and PEP screening results for UBOs, directors and major counterparties against UN, OFAC, EU and PRC sanctions lists; end-use and end-user certificates for steel structures; contracts, bills of lading, customs export declarations and commodity tariff classification certificates demonstrating civilian prefabricated building use; and a signed compliance letter undertaking not to deal with restricted countries or parties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The shareholder remits registered capital or capital reserve from its overseas bank via SWIFT MT103/MT202 to the WFOE's FDI capital account held at a Tier-1 domestic bank. The payment must identify the SAFE FDI business registration code and use the correct SAFE foreign-exchange transaction purpose code for inbound direct investment / equity contribution. The receiving bank verifies the registration code against SAFE's Foreign Direct Investment system, performs source-of-funds checks on the remitting party, and then either retains the foreign currency or converts it to RMB under the capital settlement rules. Within 60 to 90 days after injection, a licensed PRC CPA must issue a capital verification report, which is required for updating the corporate registry and later dividend distribution. The WFOE must not use capital-account funds for working capital outside the approved business scope unless such use is permissible under the SAFE capital-account settlement regulations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound EPC and steel-structure trade settlements, the WFOE should use SWIFT MT103/MT202 wire transfers for TT payments, Commercial Letters of Credit for large or documentary import/export contracts, and Documentary Collections for lower-risk open-account transactions. Each disbursement must be supported by the underlying contract, commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or air waybill, customs declaration, and import/export verification records. The bank will perform trade-in-goods authenticity checks and match the payment with SAFE's monitoring system. For cross-border services such as overseas engineering design, a tax payment certificate and service-trade purpose code are required. For RMB-denominated trade with Chinese counterparties or cross-border RMB, the WFOE may route settlement through CIPS.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore real-demand forward FX contracts for current-account receipts/payments and genuine capital-account cash flows, executed with a licensed domestic bank after SAFE risk-need assessment
FX swaps for the rollover of trade-related foreign currency cash flows, with documentary evidence of the underlying trade exposure
Vanilla and structured currency options approved by the domestic bank under SAFE's derivative qualification regime
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for hedging long-term foreign-currency debt or capital commitments

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted for onshore PRC WFOEs; only an offshore parent or non-resident affiliate may use NDFs outside China, and the WFOE must never be a party to such contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Information Report (Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June of the year following the reporting fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inclusion in the Operating Abnormal List within 10 days after June 30; failure to rectify within 3 years triggers inclusion in the Serious Illegal and Dishonest Enterprise List, administrative revocation of the business license, and a 3-year directorship/representative disqualification; fines of RMB 1,000-10,000 may apply for late reporting or false statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) jointly administered through the SAMR annual reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June of the year following the reporting fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Order of rectification with specified deadline; if the WFOE refuses to rectify, penalties range from RMB 10,000 to RMB 500,000; continued non-compliance is treated as failure to comply with the Foreign Investment Law and may trigger administrative sanctions, blacklisting, and restriction on foreign exchange capital flows.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual FDI Equity and Operation Information Report (FDI Stock Registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the annual FDI registration system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June of the year following the reporting fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance places the WFOE on SAFE's exception monitoring list; subsequent foreign exchange settlement and remittance approvals may be suspended; fines under the Foreign Exchange Administrative Provisions may reach RMB 200,000; repeated violations may trigger forced repatriation of profits and denial of future FDI registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement (Annual CIT Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (SAT) via local tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 May of the year following the tax year (the 5th month after the fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of RMB 50-2,000 per return, increased to RMB 2,000-10,000 for aggravating circumstances; late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on unpaid tax (approximately 18.25% per annum); tax authorities may block invoice issuance, enforce compulsory collection, and impose criminal liability for tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Audit Report by a Chinese CPA Firm
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of shareholders and local SAMR / SAT / MOFCOM inspection authorities upon demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed and audited financial statements presented to the shareholders no later than 30 April of the following fiscal year and before the CIT final settlement deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to complete the statutory audit exposes the WFOE to administrative supervision penalties, inclusion in the operating abnormal list, rejection of the annual enterprise credit report, tax adjustments by SAT, and potential qualification losses in tenders and bank credit facilities; willful omission may lead to criminal prosecution of the responsible officers.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under PRC Company Law Article 164 and the Foreign Investment Information Reporting System, every wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) must undergo an independent audit by a China-licensed CPA firm each year, with no minimum balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount exemption. In addition, the following quantitative triggers conclusively mandate audit: (a) total assets exceeding RMB 50 million (approximately USD 7 million); (b) annual operating revenue exceeding RMB 50 million (approximately USD 7 million); (c) average workforce exceeding 300 employees; (d) any listed debt or public-interest undertaking; (e) application for high-tech enterprise accreditation requiring audited financial statements for the preceding three years; (f) carried-forward tax losses exceeding RMB 10 million requiring audited support; and (g) related-party transactions aggregating over RMB 20 million per year, requiring transfer-pricing audit documentation. All audits must be performed in accordance with China Standards on Auditing (CSAs) issued by the Ministry of Finance.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS/CAS), which are substantially converged with IFRS for general-purpose financial statements; smaller enterprises meeting the Ministry of Finance small-enterprise scope may apply the Small Enterprise Accounting Standards (SEAS) but must still produce statutory books reconcilable to PRC GAAP; the audited financial statements serve as the base for CIT final settlement and MOFCOM/SAMR annual reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Measures for Beneficial Ownership Information Management, the WFOE must simultaneously maintain a beneficial owner register at its registered office and file beneficial ownership details with SAMR through the National Enterprise Registration System. The annual confirmation of beneficial ownership is integrated into the 1 January-30 June SAMR annual report window. Any transfer of equity, change in ultimate controlling person, or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to SAMR within 30 days from the date of the registration change. The corporate books must also record all board resolutions approving transfers and the updated member register must be kept at the registered office.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 300 - 1,200 USD for a shared-service registered address; 8,000 - 25,000 USD for a physical commercial office lease in a Tier-2 city; 20,000 - 60,000 USD for a physical office lease in Tier-1 cities such as Shanghai or Shenzhen
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2,500 - 12,000 USD for a small- to mid-sized WFOE; 25,000 - 60,000 USD for a steel-structure prefabricated building EPC manufacturer with material related-party transactions, SAFE reporting complexity, and multi-year project revenue recognition

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced CIT rate of 15% for qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises (HNTE); 15% for encouraged industries in the Western Region; preferential 10% withholding tax on non-resident dividends (not an enterprise income tax rate); reduced effective CIT of 5% for Small Low-Profit Enterprises (SLPEs) on taxable income up to RMB 3 million under the 20% preferential tax base calculation; 100% additional deduction (super-deduction) for qualified R&D expenses; Hainan Free Trade Port 15% CIT on encouraged industrial enterprises; no general patent box regime in China.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, A-type) together with supplemental schedules; filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration (STA) e-Taxation portal (etax.chinatax.gov.cn) or the local executive electronic filing system. Quarterly provisional returns use Form A200000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly provisional filing plus annual final reconciliation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly return due within 15 days after the close of each quarter (March 31, June 30, September 30, December 31); annual final return and self-assessment payment due by May 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate operating revenue from EPC engineering design, steel structure prefabrication, installation and assembly, and sales of prefabricated steel building components.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include China-source and export sales. Recompute revenue under percentage-of-completion if project methods apply; exclude value-added tax (VAT). Verify that any revenue attributable to a non-resident service provider does not create a permanent establishment (PE) exposure in China unless a filing is separately required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct raw steel and alloy costs, imported prefab components, subcontracting expenses, direct labor and plant depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border purchases from related parties must meet the arm's length standard and be documented contemporaneously. If the cost embeds imported services, confirm service withholding tax (6% VAT plus surcharges, 10% CIT if no treaty) is declared on a timely basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: City maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, local education surcharge, stamp duty on construction contracts, and resource-related levies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: VAT paid is not an enterprise income tax deduction; only sales tax surcharges and other non-CIT taxes are deductible. Late payment penalties, tax fines and criminal penalties are non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Export freight, customs clearance, overseas marketing, tender bonds, and sales commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Commissions paid to non-resident sales agents are deductible only if supported by service agreements, proof of actual service, and correct withholding. An arm's-length commission rate must be substantiated by local comparables or internal data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Management salaries, office rental, insurance, professional fees, IT, and amortization of intangible assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees from a foreign parent are deductible only when there is evidence of the actual provision of services, the costs pass a benefit test, and the fee is determined on an arm's length basis pursuant to SAT Announcement 2016 No. 42. Add back any undocumented or duplicative charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest on bank loans, intercompany borrowings, foreign exchange losses, and financing arrangement fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest on non-resident related-party debt exceeding the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin capitalization safe harbour is non-deductible and may be recharacterized as a dividend distribution, attracting 10% WHT. The interest must satisfy the arm's length rate and treaty beneficial ownership test or WHT at 10% applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting total profit as adjusted by the tax reconciliation schedule (taxable income) after applying loss carry-forwards and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible related-party expenses, excess interest, and disallowed losses; apply the 5-year loss carry-forward (10 years for qualifying high-tech or tech SME); the final taxable income should be consistent with the arm's length profit level implied by the WFOE's functions, assets and risks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule A101010 (Box 8) - Related-Party Transaction Annual Reporting
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all related-party transactions, including sales, purchases, loans, royalties and services with non-resident affiliates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be filed together with the annual CIT return whenever related-party transaction thresholds are met. Identify each non-resident related party, the jurisdiction, transaction amount and transfer pricing method used. Attach the contemporaneous Master File / Local File and be ready for a special tax adjustment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing / non-filing of quarterly or annual return: administrative fine up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000 to 10,000 in severe cases (Tax Collection Law Art. 62). Late payment: daily surcharge of 0.05% of the overdue tax (Art. 32). Understating tax through non-compliance in related-party disclosures exposes the enterprise to Special Tax Adjustment, interest penalty of 5 percentage points above the benchmark RMB lending rate, and 50%-500% fine for tax evasion. In criminal cases, the False Tax Declaration threshold may trigger criminal liability under Criminal Law Art. 201.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed by the WFOE to its non-resident corporate shareholder (CIT Law Art. 37 and State Council Decree No. 512), unless reduced under a Double Tax Agreement (DTA).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply for a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must (1) hold a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority in its home jurisdiction; (2) submit the TRC and the Chinese Non-resident Enterprise Tax Treaty Benefits Declaration Form to the tax authority in charge of the WFOE, or file the treaty benefit claim through the withholding agent before the dividend distribution; (3) demonstrate 'beneficial ownership' and substantive economic activity in the residence jurisdiction, i.e., not merely pass-through or conduit arrangement with no management, employees or assets; (4) confirm the Principal Purpose Test under the MLI is passed; and (5) retain and present board minutes, share register and distribution resolutions to substantiate ownership and entitlement. Approved DTA rates typically reduce dividends to 5% when the shareholder holds at least 25% capital in the resident enterprise for at least 12 months, or 10% otherwise for many DTA partners.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and interest paid to non-resident enterprises are each subject to a statutory 10% CIT withholding plus applicable VAT (6% on royalties, 6% or 3% on interest depending on instrument) and local surcharges. Under a DTA, rates are commonly reduced to 5-10% for interest and 5-10% for royalties, subject to beneficial ownership and Limitation on Benefits clauses. Domestic law requires the WFOE to withhold and pay within 7 days of each payment; late payments attract interest and penalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File / contemporaneous documentation must be prepared if any of the following prior-year related-party transaction thresholds are exceeded (RMB): tangible property transfer > RMB 200 million; intangible property transfer > RMB 100 million; financial asset transfers > RMB 100 million; related-party services > RMB 40 million. Master File is required when the aggregate related-party transaction amount exceeds RMB 1 billion. CbC Report is required when the ultimate parent group's consolidated revenue exceeds RMB 5.5 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not have a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) filing regime similar to offshore finance centres, but the substance-over-form principle is embedded in CIT Law Art. 47 GAAR and SAT's beneficial ownership rules. For a WFOE manufacturing steel prefabs, the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) such as procurement, production, engineering decisions, risk management and credit risk must be performed and controlled in China; if key activities are located offshore, tax authorities may reallocate profits, deny treaty benefits or apply a deemed PE. The enterprise should therefore maintain board minutes, employment records, office/factory premises, and decision logs that demonstrate actual CIGA in mainland China.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately creating false Fapiao (special VAT invoices), understating EPC contract revenue, shifting revenue to personal accounts, or inflating steel purchase costs with fictitious invoices, causing underpayment of corporate income tax and VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority will recover the underpaid taxes, charge a daily late surcharge of 0.05%, and impose a fine from 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount under Tax Collection Law Art. 63. Criminal Law Art. 201 punishes fraudulent tax evasion with up to 3 years' imprisonment if the tax evaded is relatively large, and 3 to 7 years if the amount is enormous and the evasion ratio is above 30%, plus a fine and criminal confiscation of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: When a director directs, participates in, or knowingly benefits from the fraud, the corporate veil is pierced under Company Law Art. 20; the director is jointly and severally liable for the tax and penalties, individual bank accounts and real property may be seized, and the person is placed on the tax exit-control blacklist (travel ban) under Tax Collection Law Art. 44. A director can also be criminally prosecuted as the principal offender, risking imprisonment and personal asset confiscation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Abuse and Conduit Arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Hong Kong or Singapore holding company with no commercial substance, employees, offices or decision-making, solely to channel Chinese dividends out of the WFOE so as to obtain a reduced DTA withholding rate instead of the 10% statutory rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The General Anti-Abuse Rule (CIT Law Art. 47; Implementation Regulations Arts. 120-123) authorizes tax authorities to recharacterize the arrangement; the denied treaty benefit results in re-assessed 10% or 20% withholding tax, plus late interest, and a 50%-500% penalty for under-withholding. The OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test is read into China-ratified DTAs and used to deny treaty relief if obtaining the benefit is one of the main purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who structures or participates in the conduit arrangement may be assessed personally as a responsible officer for the unpaid withholding tax and penalties when the WFOE cannot satisfy the debt; personal assets can be reached through legal authorization and asset tracing; criminal liability may arise under Criminal Law Art. 201 if the WFOE intentionally fails to withhold taxes; the director can also be blacklisted or denied exit from China under tax security control measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manipulating export prices for steel structures and prefab components sold to a related offshore buyer at artificially low prices, or paying excessive management fees and high interest on shareholder loans, leaving operations at a tax loss while shifting profits out of China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT Law Arts. 41 and 48 empower the tax authority to make a special tax adjustment using the arm's length principle; the adjustment reattributes profit to the Chinese WFOE and imposes a compensatory interest surcharge equal to the RMB benchmark lending rate plus 5 percentage points for the adjusted year, in addition to late payment charges. If the mispricing is found to be fraudulent and not merely a pricing difference, Tax Collection Law Art. 63 penalties up to 500% of the underpaid tax are applied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally approve or sign off false transfer pricing documentation or arrange sham loan/fee structures with no commercial justification can be held personally liable for the resulting tax underpayment, including the adjustment and interest; the tax authority may seek civil restitution from the director's personal fortune, impose exit restrictions (travel bans) and refer the case to criminal prosecution for evasion where the deliberate mispricing is proven. The criminal threshold is met when the suppressed profit exceeds specified monetary and tax amounts, yielding imprisonment of up to 7 years plus fines.
